extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, journal editors, and researchers studying peer review/validation practices
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of the nature and role of peer review in mathematics, focusing on typical refereeing workflows (often a single referee), how proofs are checked, and whether these practices justify current journal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review reliability in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in mathematics is relatively reliable (only one previous systematic study exists: Geist, Löwe, and Van Kerkhove 2010).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'reliability' as an evaluative benchmark when discussing mathematical peer review; comparative claims (that math is more reliable than other fields) should be supported by empirical studies or prior systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-referee review practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to mathematical journals are usually only reviewed by a single referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that single-referee workflows are common in mathematics; any assessment of journal procedures should consider this norm and whether it is justified for the kinds of validation required in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of referees' checking (not line-by-line)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent empirical studies indicate that the referees do not check the papers line by line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect selective checking rather than exhaustive, line-by-line verification. When evaluating refereeing quality, consider what parts of a paper referees focus on and that complete formal verification is often not performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof validity assessment as the core aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The common practice of mathematical journals of using just one referee is justified from the point of view of proof validity assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame referee responsibilities primarily around assessing the validity of proofs within established mathematical practice; arguments about adequate refereeing should address whether a single referee can reliably assess proof validity given disciplinary norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual embedding in mathematical validation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical practice in general and refereeing practices in particular are such that the common practice (e.g., single-referee use) is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation or reform proposals for mathematical peer review should account for broader disciplinary validation practices (norms, community verification, trust networks). Empirical/qualitative evidence (e.g., interviews — this study used interviews with seven mathematicians) is relevant to justify claims about adequacy of practices.
